findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default encryption policy.

No ACL is declared and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so it relies entirely on account defaults to prevent public ACLs or bucket policies from exposing archived reports.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.

A private ACL is set but no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a later bucket policy or ACL change could expose ledger data publicly with no account-level guardrail in this configuration.
The model artifacts bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored artifacts are not encrypted by default with a managed or customer-managed key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or bucket policies.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain infrastructure detail and occasionally embedded credentials, are stored with no server-side encryption configuration.
No public access block resource is attached, leaving the bucket dependent on account-level defaults to prevent public exposure of runbook content.

findings.issue_category: invalid canned ACL on log bucket
findings.description: The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid S3 canned ACL; the intended value is almost certainly "log-delivery-write". The apply will fail or, if tolerated, the log-delivery grant needed for access logging will not be applied, breaking the audit logging control for aws_s3_bucket.model_artifacts.
The bucket that receives access logs for other buckets has no public access block, so a misapplied ACL or policy could expose audit logs revealing object names and access patterns.

force_destroy = true on the central audit log bucket allows all audit log objects to be destroyed by a Terraform operation, and no object lock or MFA delete is configured, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.

The vendor roster object is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also has no default encryption, so this third-party data is stored without encryption at rest.
No bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is attached to the audit log bucket (nor to any bucket in this file), so log data may be written or read over unencrypted HTTP.
